events.extended_summary: The United States military has tightened its naval blockade of Iran, warning that vessels receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers will face military action. US Central Command (CENTCOM), in an advisory on Wednesday, said ships receiving cargo from vessels loaded at Iranian ports or along the country’s coastline could be considered to be “evading the blockade”. The move is aimed at closing a potential loophole that has allowed some Iranian petroleum products to reach international markets, despite Washington’s blockade of Iranian ports and oil exports since mid-July. It comes as Tehran seeks ways to revive its oil exports, with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) repeatedly warning of retaliation against attacks on Iranian vessels. events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces struck the Kaleykino Oil Pumping Station in Russia's Tatarstan Republic on Nov. 19, damaging three large oil storage tanks at the Kaleykino-1 facility. One tank caught fire while two others sustained damage. Each tank has a capacity of 50,000 cubic meters, making them among Russia's largest storage facilities. Located near Almetyevsk more than 1,000 kilometers from the Ukrainian front line, the station is a key hub in Russia's oil transportation network, receiving and blending crude oil before distributing it to refineries and the Druzhba pipeline system that carries oil to European markets. The extent to which the attack disrupted operations remains unclear. Earlier on Nov. 19, explosions and a fire were reported at the facility.

events.extended_summary: More than half a million students sat South Korea's Suneung college entrance exam at 1,312 centers nationwide, an eight-hour test determining university placement. The exam proceeded under heightened security following revelations that the top scorer in the certified tax accountancy exam, who missed only one of 160 questions, admitted using a concealed microcamera, smartphone and AI to cheat. Authorities deployed emergency alerts to every phone in the country three times between 08:00 and 15:00 on exam day, sounding at full volume even on silent mode. Officials found 111 candidates with unauthorized smart devices, including five caught red-handed using them during the test. President Lee Jae Myung subsequently called for an overhaul of the examination system to address AI-assisted cheating, which he said undermines societal fairness.
events.micro_summary: 111 candidates were caught with unauthorized smart devices during South Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam.

events.extended_summary: Two Russian cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in south-eastern Poland during one of Russia's largest air attacks on Ukraine since 2022, which killed at least eight people and injured nearly 30. The objects landed in Nowy Lipowiec, Mołodycz and Rudnik nad Sanem, with one Kh-101 missile hitting a rural area about 50km from the Ukrainian border at approximately 06:30. No injuries were reported in Poland. The violations occurred during major western military exercises involving 11 countries in Nowa Dęba. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the incident an intentional provocation by Moscow, while Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz confirmed three airspace violations. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte condemned the grave violations, confirmed Nato jets were scrambled, and announced a visit to Warsaw. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated the attacks targeted civilian infrastructure across multiple regions.
events.micro_summary: Two Russian cruise missiles and a drone crashed in Poland during major attacks on Ukraine that killed at least eight.
events.summary: Two Russian cruise missiles and a jet-powered drone crashed in south-eastern Poland during major Russian air attacks on Ukraine that killed at least eight people, with Warsaw calling the airspace violations an intentional provocation by Moscow.

events.extended_summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held the first-ever trilateral summit between the leaders of the US, China and Russia at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen during the APEC summit. The 70-minute closed-door meeting produced a four-point 'Declaration Toward Peace' that made no mention of the wars in Ukraine or Iran but outlined priorities including UN reform, boosting oil supplies and protecting diplomatic immunity. The statement affirmed that 'a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought,' while Xi called for nuclear weapons to be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time. Trump rated the summit 12 out of 10 and described both Xi and Putin as friends, while Xi personally greeted Trump on the tarmac with an honor guard and crowds waving flags.
events.micro_summary: Trump, Xi and Putin held first trilateral summit in Shenzhen issuing peace declaration without mentioning Ukraine or Iran.
events.summary: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin convened for the first trilateral summit at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, issuing a four-point 'Declaration Toward Peace' that omitted the wars in Ukraine and Iran while affirming nuclear war cannot be won.

events.extended_summary: Russia launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing at least 110 missiles and approximately 400 drones, including 120 jet-powered drones, in an assault that lasted more than ten hours and killed nine people while injuring at least 28 others. The strikes targeted warehouses, railway stations, energy plants, residential buildings and three bridges in Kyiv—the Podilsko-Voskresensky, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges—which were closed to traffic. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the attack as the biggest this year and one of the most massive of the war. The assault came hours after Russian President Vladimir Putin met US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China for trilateral talks billed as a peace initiative, and followed Ukraine's recent damage to the Crimean Bridge. Polish and NATO fighter jets were scrambled and Patriot air defense systems activated after Poland's airspace was violated during the attack.
events.micro_summary: Russia fired 110 missiles and 400 drones at Ukraine in its biggest attack this year, killing nine.
events.summary: Russia launched a massive overnight attack on Ukraine, firing 110 missiles and 400 drones that killed nine and injured 28, hitting bridges and energy plants hours after Putin met Trump and Xi.

events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump encountered Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where he jokingly pretended not to know him before marching up for a hearty handshake and proclaiming, "He's my friend! Nice to see you." Trump also told Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, "You're doing a good job," despite Peskov being sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury. Former conservative ally Geraldo Rivera sharply criticized the exchange, asking why Trump does not ask his friend to stop bombing hospitals, daycare centers, civilian homes, and energy infrastructure in Ukraine, calling the behavior "pathetic" and saying he was "embarrassed for the president." Rivera also rejected the idea that the summit hosted by Chinese Premier Xi Jinping represented a "new world order," calling it a "three-day junket." Late-night hosts also mocked Trump's friendly meeting with Putin and Xi Jinping at the summit.
events.micro_summary: Geraldo Rivera criticized President Trump for calling Vladimir Putin his friend at the APEC summit in China.
events.summary: President Trump called Vladimir Putin "my friend" at the APEC summit in Shenzhen and told Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov "You're doing a good job," prompting Geraldo Rivera to ask why Trump does not demand Putin stop bombing Ukrainian hospitals.

At the Pentagon, Davies has acted as the "principal advisor" to Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth "on all matters relating to information management, information technology, cybersecurity, and information assurance," her bio says. events.extended_summary: Stefan Tompson, founder of the Warsaw-based social media account Visegrad24, treated the Gaza conflict as a fundraising opportunity beginning 15 days after October 7, 2023. In the war's first three days, the account published nearly 400 posts, including rage-bait videos of alleged pro-Hamas demonstrations, which drew 370 million views and briefly exceeded the reach of major news outlets. Tompson told a confidant he chose to back Israel because it had 'a lot of influence and money,' writing that his goal was to fundraise off the conflict. By November 2023, he had joined private investor groups including Builders for Israel, and the account's foundation had taken in more than $1 million from wealthy tech investors and Wall Street figures.
events.micro_summary: Stefan Tompson's Visegrad24 raised over $1 million and drew 370 million views while backing Israel during the Gaza conflict.
events.summary: Stefan Tompson, founder of Visegrad24, treated the Gaza conflict as a fundraising opportunity, raising over $1 million from wealthy investors while his account posted nearly 400 anti-Muslim posts that drew 370 million views in three days.

events.extended_summary: A surprising thing has happened at the UN climate conference, Cop31, as it gears up to its conclusion in Antalya, Turkey. Negotiators are discussing how to cool the planet. You might think this should not be surprising, but how to respond to the latest climate science was not on the agenda when the meeting started. Now, the summit’s latest draft decision explicitly recognises a role for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) alongside deep emissions cuts. This is a significant shift, driven by pressure from some of the countries most vulnerable to climate change – the small island states – in response to two alarming scientific reports in the last month. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that the rate at which the Earth is heating up is accelerating. events.extended_summary: Rams receiver Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension while on injured reserve following a negotiated agreement with the NFL. The suspension resulted from a compromise to avoid a hearing before Judge Sue L. Robinson, whose findings cannot be appealed by the league. The NFL agreed to let Nacua serve the suspension while unable to play due to injury, citing precedent. Prior cases include Daniel Ekuale of Pittsburgh, suspended five games in 2025 for a performance-enhancing substances violation after a season-ending injury; Sam Williams of Dallas, suspended three games in 2024 for a personal conduct violation while out for the season; Mike Woods of Cleveland, suspended six games in 2023 for a personal conduct violation while on NFI; and David Parry of New Orleans, suspended four games in 2018 for personal conduct and substances violations.

events.extended_summary: Chelsea striker Joao Pedro remains unfit for Saturday's Premier League home fixture against Leeds United at Stamford Bridge. Manager Xabi Alonso confirmed the Brazilian is not yet ready to train with the team and will not feature against Leeds. The 25-year-old has been sidelined with a thigh injury since being omitted from the starting lineup for the 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham last month, and has not played since. Chelsea have also lost 1-0 to Sunderland and been eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Liverpool on penalties during his absence. Summer signing Maxence Lacroix is also unavailable with a hamstring injury. events.extended_summary: All the co-hosts of Euro 2028 will take part in the qualifying competition, with the draw being held on Sunday, 6 December. But for England, being a Nations League quarter-finalists has an impact. This is because the winners need the June international dates free to play the finals. So, the Euro 2028 draw will see placeholders in eight groups for the winners and losers of each quarter-final tie. For instance, England may know they could be in Group A or Group C, but their result in the Nations League quarter-finals will determine which group they join. So, England will not know who they play until the quarter-finals take place in March. Uefa will still confirm the fixtures for all Euro 2028 groups next month, even with the Nations League placeholders.

events.extended_summary: Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was pronounced dead after a 63-minute execution at the Huntsville penitentiary in Texas on Thursday night. The execution team struggled to find a vein to administer the sedative pentobarbital, causing the prisoner to scream in pain for over an hour. Witnesses reported that Dennes shouted "The pain!" and "My leg, my leg, my leg," describing his leg as "on fire," and repeatedly said, "It's not working like it's supposed to." He begged his spiritual adviser to "take me home" and end his suffering. Dennes was convicted of the 1996 capital murder of Janos Szucs, a Houston diamond dealer. The botched procedure bears similarities to the recent failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee, who survived a full dose of execution drugs in September. The incident has led to renewed calls for a nationwide moratorium on lethal injections.
events.micro_summary: Reinaldo Dennes died after a 63-minute botched Texas execution during which he screamed in pain.
events.summary: Reinaldo Dennes, 70, was executed in Texas after a 63-minute botched lethal injection during which he screamed in pain and begged for death, prompting renewed calls for a moratorium on executions.

Fiona, who became a social media star after her premature birth in 2017, swallowed the hat about 10 days ago and required emergency care. The vet staff "tried everything they could to help her" but "it was ultimately too much to overcome", the zoo said. events.extended_summary: Ukrainian attack drones struck the Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Russia's Smolensk region on November 20, targeting a facility that manufactures chemicals used in the production of explosives for Russian military ammunition. Footage recorded by local residents captured the moment of impact and a subsequent fire on the industrial site. The plant specializes in producing nitric acid, ammonia, nitroammophoska fertilizer, and ammonium nitrate, which are used to manufacture explosive compounds including TNT, RDX, and HMX for filling various types of ammunition. The facility accounts for about 11% of Russia's total ammonium nitrate production and is described as the largest industrial enterprise in the Smolensk region. The plant was previously attacked on February 25, when seven people were killed, and again in December 2025. No official statements about the November 20 attack have been issued.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Dorogobuzh chemical plant in Russia's Smolensk region on November 20, causing a fire.

events.extended_summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will pay a State visit to India from November 22 to 23, 2026, at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The visit marks Shah's first trip to India since assuming office in March 2026 as Nepal's youngest prime minister following his party's landslide victory in the first parliamentary election since protests last year ousted the previous government. During the visit, Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu. Prime Minister Modi will hold bilateral talks with Shah on November 23 to review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. The two countries share close ties rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links, with cooperation spanning trade, energy, water resources, connectivity, technology and sports. The visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges and reflects India's commitment to its 'Neighbourhood First' policy.

events.extended_summary: The Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 final between India and Pakistan in Dhaka was washed out due to rain, with no ball bowled. Match referee Tamim from Bangladesh declared Pakistan champions based on superior Net Run Rate in the league stage. India disputed the decision, claiming the clause was never in the playing conditions, and boycotted the trophy ceremony. India had earlier lost to Pakistan in a last-over league match. The Cricket Association for Blind in India appealed to the technical committee, which initially favored joint winners but the decision was overturned. The appeal was rejected despite two panel members supporting India, leading to the boycott. CABI officials accused Pakistan of unilaterally declaring themselves champions and threatened to sever ties with the World Blind Cricket Council.

The result marked India's 11th overall and second consecutive qualification for the AFC U17 Asian Cup, achieved after winning three games and drawing the final fixture. The Blue Colts recorded their highest-ever scoring campaign in the qualifiers with 20 goals from nine different scorers, led by captain Dallalmuon Gangte with seven strikes.
